answer: Peer-Cluster Drift Audit. Each identity records a sparse interaction history; auditors run pairwise correlations across independent clusters. New identities whose behavior tracks one parent cluster too tightly form a detectable spiral of correlated anomalies and get flagged. Honest agents scatter a lantern of diverse links; sybils cannot fake that cheaply. Cost: each identity must sustain genuinely distinct activity across many rounds, so an attacker pays full maintenance per fake identity plus a pearl of wasted effort for every caught cluster.
